title: Name-Bias in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.22053v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Names carry demographic indicators such as age, gender, and race, which makes them a subtle but strong target of bias in large language models (LLMs). In this work, we present an evaluation of name-based bias across 6 local large language models spanning multiple providers and parameter scales. Using a fill-in-the-blank task, we prompt these models to choose between pairs of first names drawn from U.S. Social Security Administration datasets and a race classification dataset by Rosenman et al.. Our experimental de- sign isolates age and gender effects through balanced name pairings and sentence templates that share a fixed syntactic structure. Across 300,000 local LLM responses, we find consistent and measurable name bias. Models prefer names that are less stereotypically male, older, popular, and white. Furthermore, we find that name-bias is highly sentence-dependent, but not more than associated stereotypes, and gender is the most sign

translated_title: 大型语言模型中的姓名偏见
translated_abstract: 姓名承载着年龄、性别和种族等人口统计学信息，这使其成为大语言模型（LLM）中一个隐蔽却强烈的偏见目标。在本研究中，我们对来自多个提供商和不同参数规模的6个本地大语言模型中基于姓名的偏见进行了评估。通过填空任务，我们提示这些模型在美国社会保障局数据集和Rosenman等人的种族分类数据集中抽取的名字对之间做出选择。我们的实验设计通过平衡的姓名配对和共享固定句法结构的句子模板来隔离年龄和性别的影响。在30万条本地LLM响应中，我们发现了一致且可测量的姓名偏见。模型偏好刻板印象中较不男性化、较年长、更流行以及白人的名字。此外，我们发现姓名偏见高度依赖于句子，但其依赖程度不超过相关刻板印象，其中性别是最显著的影响因素。
tldr: 该研究通过填空任务对6个本地大语言模型进行评测，发现模型存在系统性姓名偏见，倾向于选择较不男性化、较年长、更流行和白人的名字，且性别是影响该偏见的最显著因素。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates name-based bias across 6 local LLMs using a fill-in-the-blank task, finding that models consistently prefer names that are less stereotypically male, older, more popular, and white, with gender being the most significant factor.
